Before in-person training

    Safety

    • Steam model: the air hose connects to the lab’s compressed air supply. Supply only a small amount of air, or the hose will blow.
    • Stirling models: the flame and the hot end stay hot for a while after use. Let them cool before touching, and keep hair and loose sleeves clear of the flywheels.
    • Part II (the RC cars) is run by Active Learning Labs staff unless a TF volunteers.

    Walk through the models

    Pick a model. Use the numbered steps to play each stage of its cycle, then tap the dots on the photo to find the matching parts on the bench.

    Heat applied from outsideFuel burns inside

    Compare engines

    Every engine here is a heat engine: compress a gas, add heat, let it expand, then reject heat. Choose the engines you want to compare to see where each step happens in each one.

    Check your understanding

    Eight quick questions, the kind students tend to ask. Answers explain themselves.

    The animated diagrams are simplified schematics: they show the sequence of events, not true proportions, timing or pressures.
